title: Impact of COPS Grant on Violent Crime Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with unit and time fixed effects.  
Why: Some municipalities (treated = 1) receive the COPS hiring grant while others do not.  The grant starts to matter only in the post periods (post = 1).  Comparing the change in log violent-crime rates of treated municipalities before versus after receipt with the contemporaneous change in control municipalities gives the causal effect, provided that—absent the grant—both groups would have followed parallel trends.

Key assumptions  
1. Parallel-trends: In the absence of COPS funding, treated and control municipalities would have experienced the same evolution in violent-crime rates.  
2. No spillovers: COPS funding to one municipality does not directly affect crime in another.  
3. Stable treatment timing: Each treated municipality begins receiving the grant at one clearly defined time (reflected by post = 1).  

## 2. R Code
```r
# Required packages
library(readr)     # fast CSV reader
library(dplyr)     # data wrangling
library(fixest)    # high-performance fixed-effects estimation
library(ggplot2)   # visualisation for robustness

# 1. Read the data -------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s46_data.csv",
               col_types = cols())   # let readr guess the types

# Quick check
print(head(df, 3))
cat("Unique municipalities:", n_distinct(df$unit_id), "\n")
cat("Periods:", paste0(range(df$period), collapse = " – "), "\n")

# 2. Baseline DID with two-way fixed effects -----------------------------------
did_base <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                  data    = df,
                  cluster = ~unit_id)      # cluster at municipality level

cat("\n=== Baseline DID ===\n")
print(summary(did_base))

# 3. Robustness check 1: allow for heteroskedasticity-robust SEs only ----------
did_hc  <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                 data = df, se = "hetero")
cat("\n=== Robustness 1: Heteroskedasticity-robust SEs ===\n")
print(summary(did_hc))

# 4. Robustness check 2: Event-study to test pre-trends ------------------------
# Build treatment-onset (cohort) variable = first period when post == 1
df <- df %>%
  group_by(unit_id) %>%
  mutate(cohort = ifelse(any(post == 1 & treated == 1),
                         min(period[post == 1 & treated == 1]),
                         0L)) %>%          # cohort = 0 for never-treated
  ungroup()

# Event-study using Sun & Abraham (2021) estimator
es <- feols(y ~ sunab(cohort, period) | unit_id + period,
            data    = df,
            cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n=== Robustness 2: Event-Study (Sun-Abraham) ===\n")
print(summary(es, nvalues = 4))   # show a few leads/lags

# Plot the dynamic effects -----------------------------------------------------
iplot(es, ref.line = 0) +
  labs(title = "Event-Study: Effect of COPS Grant on Log Violent Crime",
       y = "Estimate (log-points)", x = "Periods relative to grant receipt")

# 5. Output the key numerical result ------------------------------------------
att <- coef(did_base)["treat_x_post"]
se  <- se(did_base)["treat_x_post"]
cat(sprintf("\nATT (log-points) = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f , %.4f]\n",
            att, se, att - 1.96*se, att + 1.96*se))
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative.  COPS hiring grants increase sworn-officer staffing, which should lower violent-crime rates.  In log terms, prior literature suggests a 5–10 % decline, i.e. an ATT of roughly −0.05 to −0.10 log-points.  The event-study should show flat pre-treatment coefficients (supporting parallel trends) and increasingly negative post-treatment effects.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in violent crime rates between municipalities that received the grant and those that did not, before and after the grant allocation.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis reveals a positive effect of the COPS grant on the violent crime rate.
